title: Kullervo: The Cheat-Cake
subtitle: An insult to a knife sparks retaliation

learningObjectives.text: What does Kullervo call the loaf after finding the stone?

knife.author: Elias Lönnrot, compiler and editor
knife.locator: Rune XXXIII · Kullervo and the Cheat-cake; Rune XXXIII · Kullervo and the Cheat-cake, normalized characters 2870-3163
knife.excerpt: This, the blade that I hold sacred, This the one thing that I honor, Relic of my mother’s people! On the stone within this oat-loaf, On this cheat-cake of the hostess, I my precious knife have broken. How shall I repay this insult, How avenge this woman’s malice, What the wages for deception?
knife.note: Verbatim English verse translated by John Martin Crawford from Lönnrot's nineteenth-century compilation of oral poetry; not a transcript of one ancient or single oral witness.

narrativeBlocks.title: A broken knife
narrativeBlocks.body: In Rune XXXIII, Kullervo cuts into his oat-loaf and breaks the knife he values. He discovers a stone hidden inside the cake.

narrativeBlocks.title: Kullervo names the insult
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (Crawford's English translation; whitespace normalized): “This, the blade that I hold sacred, This the one thing that I honor, Relic of my mother’s people! On the stone within this oat-loaf, On this cheat-cake of the hostess, I my precious knife have broken. How shall I repay this insult, How avenge this woman’s malice, What the wages for deception?”

narrativeBlocks.title: Anger turns toward revenge
narrativeBlocks.body: Kullervo calls the loaf a cheat-cake and asks what the wages for deception should be. The next lines carry his retaliation into the herd.

narrativeBlocks.title: A named rune in a compiled epic
narrativeBlocks.body: The episode is from Lönnrot's Kalevala as translated by Crawford, not a direct transcript of a single oral performance. Kullervo's story must stay inside this version and sequence.

narrativeBlocks.title: A small object carries history
narrativeBlocks.body: Kullervo calls the knife a relic of his mother's people; the broken blade makes the meal an insult with personal and family meaning.
